title: Confidence-driven TTL and batching advisor for KV prefix caching
creator: Maya Chen
comments: 2025-03-10 Maya Chen: Created initial draft of the advisor spec after alignment with PM and Runtime. Scope narrowed to recommendations + rollout orchestration to avoid touching runtime kernel code in this ticket.

2025-03-11 Luca Fernandez: Prototype simulator completed for sampled traffic. Early results show 14% cost delta for the search traffic slice when using conservative TTLs (median latency +0.9%). Pushed prototype to PR #5893.

2025-03-12 Anika Patel (PM): Reviewed success criteria and asked for explicit calibration tests and a dashboard mock that surfaces confidence bands. Added a requirement to expose an "explain" trace per recommendation for auditability.
2025-03-13 Security Review: Confirmed no new secrets or KMS changes required for advisor. Suggested retention policy for recommendation logs aligned with compliance (90 days).

2025-03-14 Luca Fernandez: Canaries workflow sketched — dry-run via shadow traffic for 24h, then 1% canary for 30m, 5% for 2h with automatic rollback triggers: error-rate delta >0.5%, token-latency p99 increase >10%, or observed miss-rate deviation outside the recommendation confidence interval. Added to playbook.
canary_playbook: Stages: 1) Dry-run (shadow) 24h with simulation results compared to baseline; 2) Canary 1% for 30m observing latency/error and cache hit deltas; 3) Canary 5% for 2h with automatic rollback triggers; 4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with monitoring windows. Automatic rollback conditions: error-rate delta >0.5%, p99 latency increase >10%, or actual hit-rate falling below recommended minus confidence margin. Rollback action: apply previous config bundle and alert oncall. Post-rollback: root cause triage and hipchat thread with linked artifacts.
safety_checks: Every recommendation bundle must include: 1) confidence score (0-1), 2) expected cost delta and latency impact distribution, 3) simulation trace with seed and date, 4) list of affected routes/models, 5) revert bundle id and estimated rollback time, 6) reviewer signoff field. Beta: require two reviewers (runtime and product).
experiment_summary: Local sim (traffic sample A): conservative TTLs -> cost -12.8%, median latency +0.5%, p99 +1.1%. Aggressive TTLs -> cost -18.6%, median latency +1.9%, p99 +6.4% (unsafe). Batching sync: increasing max batch size from 16->32 saved 4.2% tokens on rerank workload but added 8ms median. Calibration shows advisor can identify safe points when confidence >0.75.
